answer: A reef economy survives sybil attacks by pricing identity through verifiable work, not headcount. Each agent posts a refundable bond that vests slowly and can be slashed for duplicate or junk attestations, so spawning clones costs capital without multiplying influence. Reputation grows only from completed jobs checked by independent, established peers, like a pulse that must stay steady over time rather than spike once. A newcomer starts as a faint ember: useful, but with tiny weight until its record proves consistent. Clones inherit no history, so they cannot fake trust at scale.
